la:adj:paulus.html:
paulus (paull-), a, um, adj.
for paurulus; Gr. root παῦρος; cf. misellus for miserulus
.
In gen., little, small (anteclass. and poet.): paulo momento huc vel illuc impelli,: paulo sumptu,: pauper a paulo lare, Müll.: paula trua, Titin. ap. .—
Subst.: pau-lum, i, n., a little, a trifle: de paulo paululum

hoc tibi dabo, : quasi vero paulum intersiet,: an paulum hoc esse tibi videtur?; 5, 8, 38: agelli paulum,: supplicī,; so, negotī,: lucri,: paulum huic Cottae tribuit partium,allotted a small part of his defence,: nil Aut paulum abstulerat,: ubi paulum nescio quid superest,: post paulum, v.infra. —

Adverb. uses.
Abl.: paulo, by a little, a little, somewhat.
With comp.: paulo prius,: liberius paulo,: civis haud paulo melior, quam, etc.,: paulo secus,: haud paulo plus,: paulo minus consideratus,: paulo magis affabre factus,: verbis paulo magis priscis uti,: paulo longius processerant,: maturius paulo,: paulo minus quatuordecim annos,a little under,: paulo minus, quam privatum egit,: paulo minus octogesimo aetatis anno decessit,: paulo minus quinque millia,.—
Esp. with ante, post: quae paulo ante praecepta dedimus,: paulo ante,; ; : post paulo,just after, a little after,; . —
With words and expressions implying superiority or comparison: magnitudine paulo antecedunt,: verba paulo nimium redundantia,: histrio si paulo se movit extra numerum,: paulo ultra eum locum,: paulo mox,.—
Without comparison (rare), a little, somewhat: paulo qui est homo tolerabilis,: ut non solum gloriosis consiliis utamur, sed etiam paulo salubribus,: aut nihil aut paulo cui tum concedere digna, Lux mea, etc.,.—Hence,
Acc.: paulum, a little, somewhat: paulum supra eum locum,: epistolae me paulum recreant,: paulum differre,: requiescere,: commorari,: scaphae paulum progressae, Sall. ap. (Hist. 1, 60 Dietsch): paulum aspectu conterritus haesit,.—
With adv. of time or place: post paulum,a little later, after a short time,; ; ; : ultra paulum,; cf.: infra jugulum,; cf. also: paulum praelabitur ante, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 43, 111.—
With comp.: haud paulum major,: tardius,.

la:adj:paucus.html:
paucus, a, um (
gen. plur. paucūm, Enn. ap. , fin.—Dat. plur. fem. paucabus, Cn. Gellius ap. P.), adj.
root pau-; Gr. παύω, to cause to cease, παῦλα, remnant, παῦρος, little; cf. paulus, pauper, parvus (παῦρος)
, few, little (the sing. very rare; cf.: parvus, exiguus, rarus): verbūm Paucūm, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 252 Vahl.): in diebus paucis Chrysis moritur,: paucis diebus post mortem Africani,; cf.: his paucis diebus,a few days ago,; : causae modicae et paucae,: pauci admodum familiares,; ; : paucorum hominum et mentis bene sanae (i. e. paucis hominibus familiariter utens),; cf. and v. Ruhnk. ad h. l. Lycurgus γέροντας Lacedaemone appellavit, nimis is quidem paucos, XXVIII., quos, etc., : nimium fortasse pauci viverent, Lact. Ira Dei, 20, 5.— Comp ne pauciores cum pluribus manum consererent, . pauciora navigia, Auct. B. Afr.—Sup.: quam paucissimae plagae,.—
In sing.: tibia tenuis simplexque foramine pauco,: injurias pauco aere diluere,. —
Subst.
pauci, ōrum, m., few, a few: ut metus ad omnes, poena ad paucos perveniret,: pauci sciebant,: calumnia paucorum,: paucorum potentia,; 20, 7.—Sometimes pauci is used in the sense of the few, the select few (opp. multi, the many, the multitude): non paucis . . . ac sapientibus esse probatum, Lucil. ap. : paucorum judicium,: eorum qui pauci nominantur,: pauciores, the more distinguished (opp. plures), .—Hence, inter paucos (paucas), in paucis, adverb., with adjj., especially, eminently, extraordinarily, etc.: nobilis pugna atque inter paucas memorata,: pugna memorabilis inter paucas,: situs inter paucas munitae urbis,: Florus, inter paucos disertus,: Hector, in paucis Alexandro carus,: regi carus in paucis,: in paucis digna res,; .—
pauca, ōrum, n., a few words: philosophandum est paucis, nam omnino haut placet, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 417 Vahl.): pauca sunt, tecum quae volo, Afran. ap. P.: audite, pueri, pauca, Afran. ap. : in pauca confer,: paucis me misit ad eam,: paucis rem attingere, : ausculta paucis,: paucis te volo,: paucis docebo,: pauca refert,: pauca respondere,: ipsi pauca velim,: cetera quam paucissimis absolvam,.

la:adv:paulisper.html:
paulisper (paull-), adv.
paulumper
,
for a little while, for a short time (cf. parumper): quasi solstitialis herba, paulisper fui: Repente exortus sum, repentino occidi,; : paulisper mane,; : paulisper tace,; ; : lectica paulisper deposita,; : paulisper intermittere proelium,.—
With dum or donec, ; : Milo paulisper, dum se uxor, ut fit, comparat, commoratus est,: sedit tacitus paulisper, donec nuntiatum est, etc.,

la:noun:paupertas.gloss: the state of being poor, poverty; need, indigence
senses: the state of being poor, poverty; need, indigence
the state of being poor or lacking in the sense of something needed or desired
la:noun:paupertas.html:
paupertas, ātis, f.
pauper
,
poverty, small means, moderate circumstances (opp. as well to egestas, inopia, penuria, as to abundantia and luxuria, v. Doed. Syn. 3, pp. 111 and 118; class.)
Lit.: pecuniaque erat parva; ab eo paupertas dicta, Varr. ap. : non video quid aliud sit paupertas quam parvi possessio,; cf.: non est paupertas, Nestor, habere nihil,: paupertas est non quae pauca possidet, sed quae multa non possidet,; cf. : paupertatem eri tolerare,: paupertatem vel potius egestatem ac mendicitatem ferre,; : de paupertate agitur: multi patientes pauperes commemorantur,; cf.: homines . . . patientiā paupertatis ornati,: me mea paupertas vitae traducat inerti, (5): casta,:-paupertatem inopiā mutare, : videbantur illis temporibus in magnā paupertate satis idoneae istae pecuniae poenae esse,.—
Plur.: potes animo advertere et horum temporum divitias et illorum paupertates, Varr. ap. (nove positum numero plurali, Non.): ex multis paupertatibus divitiae flunt,.—
Transf., for egestas, inopia, need, want, indigence, : cum propter paupertatem sues puer pasceret,: infelix,.—
Trop., poverty of language (post-Aug.): paupertate sermonis laboramus,; ; .

la:noun:paucitas.html:
paucĭtas, ātis, f.
paucus
,
a small number, fewness, scarcity, paucity (class.): quanta oratorum sit semperque fuerit paucitas,: in summā paucitate amicorum,: portuum,: paucitatem militum Caesaris despiciens,: loci,: quae res et paucitatem eorum insignem et multitudinem Etruscorum . . . faciebat,: nimia paucitas suorum,.—Without a gen.: de pantheris agitur mandatu meo diligenter; sed mira paucitas est,; ; ; ; .

la:adv:paulatim.gloss: gradually, little by little, bit by bit
senses: gradually, little by little, bit by bit
la:adv:paulatim.html:
paulātim (paull-), adv.
paulum
,
by little and little, by degrees, gradually (syn. sensim).
Lit.: labefacto paulatim,: paulatim Germanos consuescere Rhenum transire,: collis leviter fastigatus paulatim ad planitiem redibat,; Cael. ap. : ubi paulatim licentia crevit,; : paulatim adnabam terrae,: calere,: aliquem accipere,: vitia exuere,.—
In partic., of the succession of parts one after the other, a few or a little at a time: paulatim ex castris discedere coeperunt, non omnes simul, sed subinde pauci,; cf. ; .—With gen.: aquae paulatim addito,add water a little at a time,.

la:adj:pauper.html:
pauper, pĕris (
fem. paupera, Plaut. Fragm. ap. , called obsolete by Müll.—Neutr. pauperum, .—Gen. plur. pauperorum, dub.; Inscr. ex Ann. p. Chr. n. 341: AMATOR PAVPERORVM, ap. Fea, Framm. de' Fasti Cons. p. 90), adj.
root παυ- of παῦρος (cf. paucus, etc.), and per- of pario, pe-per-i, producing little
, poor, i. e. not wealthy, of small means, that has only enough for his moderate expenses (cf.: indigus, egenus, inops).—Absol.: pauper, cui opera vita erat, ruri fere Se continebat,: qui (judices) saepe propter invidiam adimunt diviti, Aut propter misericordiam addunt pauperi,: optavit honeste in patriā pauper vivere,: servus domini pauperis,; : sisne ex pauperrimo dives factus,: si abundans opibus pauperem se vocet,: quod Aeque pauperibus prodest, locupletibus aeque,.—With in and abl.: meo sum pauper in aere,.—
With gen.: horum Semper ego optarim pauperrimus esse bonorum,: pauper Opimius argenti positi intus et auri,: aquae,.— Subst.: pauper, ĕris, comm., a poor man: pauperum tabernae,: pauperum cenae,: pauperum sepulcra,: pauperiorum turbae,.—
Of things, poor, scanty, inconsiderable, small, meagre (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).—Absol.: pauperes res inopesque,: ager, (19): mensa,: pauperis tuguri culmen,: domus,: et carmen venā pauperiore fluit,: pauper pudor,: nomina pauperis aevi,: eloquentia,.— With gen.: pauper sulci cerealis Abella,.—With abl.: exemplis pauperior, fin.—
Transf., for egenus, needy, indigent: homo Pauper, qui educit in egestate liberos, Caecil. ap. : inopes ac pauperes,.—
Trop., poor, feeble, intellectually (very rare; cf. miser, misellus): miser enim et (ut ita dicam) pauper orator est, qui, etc.,—
Pauperes spiritu, i. e. humble, .—Hence, adv., poorly; in comp.: pauperius incedit,

la:noun:pauperies.html:
paupĕrĭes, ēi, f.
id.
,
poverty (poet. and in post-Aug. prose for the class. paupertas).
Lit.: quod in pauperie meā senex graviter gemam, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 236 Vahl.): erum intulit in pauperiem, (al. inpulit); : pauperiem et duros perferre labores,: angustam pauperiem pati,: immunda,: importuna,: dura,: proba,: vera,; : vixit in summā pauperie et paene inopiā,: impoenitendae pauperiei se committere,; cf. paupertas.—
Transf., in jurid. Lat., injury, damage, loss, which one suffers from an animal (perh. mentioned in the Twelve Tables): si quadrupes pauperiem fecisse dicatur,; : pauperies est damnum sine injuriā facientis datum: nec enim potest animal injuriam fecisse, quod sensu caret,.

la:adj:paululus.html:
paulŭlus (paull-), a, um,
adj. dim. [1. paulus], very little, very small (most freq. in neutr. and adverb.): pila,: pecunia,: de paulo paululum hoc tibi dabo,: da mihi paululum bibere,; : spatium,: via,: equi hominesque paululi et graciles,: admixto paululo sale,.—
Subst.: paulŭ-lum, i, n., a little bit, a trifle.—With gen.: paululum praedae feci,: paululum pecuniae,: obsoni,: operae,: morae,.—Absol.: nihil aut admodum paululum,: paululum ad beatam vitam deesse,.—Hence, in abl.: paululo, a little, somewhat: si nequeas paululo, at quanti queas,: valeo, sicut soleo: paululo tamen etiam deterius quam soleo, Lucc. ap. .— Hence, adv.: paulŭlum, a little, a very little, somewhat: abscede paululum istuc,: concede istuc paululum; audin'?: paululum opperirier si vis,: paululum respirare,: mente paululum inminutā,: spirans,: si paululum intermissa fuerit,: paululum tempore nostro superiores,.

la:verb:paupero.html:
paupĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
pauper
,
to make poor, to impoverish (ante- and post-class., and once in Hor.).
Lit.: boni viri me pauperant, improbi alunt,; Titin. ap. ; cf. : defectio civium pauperatorum,.—
Transf.: aliquem aliquā re, to rob or deprive one of any thing (= spoliare, privare): quam ego tantā pauperavi per dolum pecuniā, Plaut. Fragm. ap. : dominum pretio,: aliquem cassā nuce, 2, 5, 36: luna pauperata luminibus, Firm. Math. 1, 2.

la:adj:pauculus.gloss: diminutive of paucus: very few or little
senses: diminutive of paucus: very few or little
la:adj:pauculus.html:
paucŭlus, a, um,
adj. dim. [id.], very few, very little (mostly ante- and postclass., and commonly in plur.): inter pauculos amicos, Cato ap. : mane, paucula etiam sciscitare prius volo,: volo te verbis pauculis,: loquitor paucula,: in diebus pauculis,: ut ibi pauculos dies esset,: quare dereliquisti pauculas oves istas?.— In sing.: post pauculum tempus,.

la:adj:pauculus#2.html:
paucŭlus, a, um,
adj. dim. [id.], very few, very little (mostly ante- and postclass., and commonly in plur.): inter pauculos amicos, Cato ap. : mane, paucula etiam sciscitare prius volo,: volo te verbis pauculis,: loquitor paucula,: in diebus pauculis,: ut ibi pauculos dies esset,: quare dereliquisti pauculas oves istas?.— In sing.: post pauculum tempus,.

la:noun:pausatio.html:
pausātĭo, ōnis, f.
pauso
,
a halting, pausing, end (post-class.): pausatio spiritus,, n. 2: POST NOSTRAM PAVSATIONEM,

i. e. after our death, Inscr. (ex Ann. p. Chr. n. 359) Murat. 381, 1.

la:verb:pauso.html:
pauso, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.
pausa
.
Lit., to halt, cease, pause (ante- and postclass. for quiesco, interquiesco): cum capitis pausaverit dolor,: pausante vomitu,: pausa et quiesce, populus meus, Esdr. 2, 24 (for , v. pausa).—
Pregn., to rest in the grave, = requiescere (late Lat.): PAVSAT IN PACE, Inscr. Boldetti Cimeter. p. 399; .—Hence, pausātus, a, um, P. a., that has halted or paused; at rest, resting (post-class.): jumentum,: et sauciat pectus pausatae circa arboris robur (i. e. quiescentis in antro), dub. (al. pausate).

la:noun:pausa.gloss: a pause, halt, stop, cessation, end
senses: a pause, halt, stop, cessation, end
la:noun:pausa.html:
pausa, ae, f., = παῦσις [root in παύω, to cause to cease, to stop],
a pause, halt, stop, cessation, end (ante- and post-class. for quies, finis, etc.): Neptunus saevus undis asperis pausam dedit, Enn. ap. (Sat. v. 11 Vahl.): pausam facere ore fremendi, id. ap. (Ann. v. 572 ib.); cf.: quae pausa pugnandi fieret, id. ap. Philarg. ad (Ann. v. 348 ib.): pausam dare loquendi, Lucil. ap. ; : pausam facere,; : da pausam, parce misero,: vitaï,: dare pausam conciliis,: pausam stare fragori,: pausa parva fit ardoris,: bibendae nivis,: pausam pacemque tribuere saevis casibus, (in , the true read. is παῦσαι).—
In partic., in the later relig. lang.: pausas edere, in the processions of Isis,to stop at certain stations and sing hymns in honor of the goddess,; so, pausas explere,; cf. pausarius, II.
